body:
This is **not** a bug.

When you set `max_fps = 30`, you limit the time between rendered frames to about `0.033` seconds.
At the same time, physics is configured with `physics_ticks_per_second = 60`, which means the physics step is `0.016` seconds.

During one rendered frame, enough real time passes for two physics steps, but after executing the first physics step (0.016 s), the engine hits the limit `max_physics_steps_per_frame = 1` and is not allowed to execute the second one. The extra physics time is discarded.

As a result, the simulation only advances by `0.016` seconds for that frame, so `_process(delta)` receives `0.016`, even though about `0.033` seconds of real time have passed.

If you change `physics_ticks_per_second`, you can observe the game speeding up or slowing down.

`delta` is the time that has passed between two frames inside the game simulation, not the time that has passed in the real world.
